subject: Mutual Action Plan kickoff — Renewal & expansion alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fasthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan kickoff — Renewal & expansion alignment

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time last week. I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) to align on stakeholders, success criteria, and the close timeline for FastHealth's renewal + potential upgrade to Dedicated. Key points in the attached:

- Proposed goals: maintain current latency SLOs, increase inference throughput for batch exports by 3x, and validate cost/benefit of a Dedicated pool for Nightly jobs.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency under 180ms for 512-token gen, embedding throughput >= 1.5k/s during peak, and <=10% monthly cost delta vs hosted baseline (after batching/quantization).
- Timeline (proposed): evaluation window 2 weeks (tech + security), procurement signatures by mid-December, targeted rollout early January.

Attachments: FastHealth_MAP_v0.1.xlsx, Q3_usage_summary.csv (export from Console).

Can you confirm the stakeholder roster on your side and whether the procurement timeline above looks feasible? Also, do you want a technical deep-dive (1–2 hours) or a short demo focused on the Dedicated upgrade path?

If it helps, I can loop Naomi from CS to coordinate the usage review and a proposed upsell plan.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fasthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Cheng <sam@fasthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan kickoff — Renewal & expansion alignment

Ben —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers:

- Stakeholders: Me (Procurement + Sponsor), Sam Cheng (Tech lead — will own evaluation), and I’ll pull in our security lead if the plan requires SOC2 docs.
- Procurement timeline: mid-December is tight but possible if procurement gets the updated commercial terms by next week.
- Technical deep-dive: Sam prefers a focused 90-minute session where we validate inference performance on our representative payloads rather than a full demo.

A couple of questions from our side: what’s the expected uplift in token-cost after switching to a Dedicated pool for the same throughput? Also, can you share any recent latency runs for 512/1024 token scenarios?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Product Operations | FastHealth Systems
elena.ruiz@fasthealth.com

Elena / Sam —

Great — thanks for the quick turn. I’ve invited Naomi from CS to oversee the usage validation and the upsell sequencing; she’ll lead the detailed runbook so your team doesn’t have to manage run configs.

For your questions:
- Token-cost: Dedicated removes per-token networking overhead and gives predictable throughput; based on comparable customers, list-to-dedicated delta varies but we typically see 5–12% unit-cost increase before batching and KV cache optimizations. Our Optimize team will run model/quant config to find savings that usually offset that.
- Latency runs: I’ve attached a short export (Q3_usage_summary.csv) and we’ll provide a latency report during the technical session. Rishi can share a 512/1024 benchmark in the meeting.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech session — 90 minutes — pick two windows next week (Nov 30 or Dec 2).
2) Naomi will ask for 48-hour access to a small traffic sample (SANITIZED) to run a quick prefix cache experiment.
3) We’ll update the MAP with targeted milestones and commercial ask for procurement by Dec 1.

Please confirm which tech session slot works and whether Sam can share example payloads ahead of time.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan kickoff — Renewal & expansion alignment

Elena / Ben —

I’ll lead the technical session. Suggested agenda (90 mins):
- 0–10m: Introductions & success criteria (Ben/Elena)
- 10–35m: Benchmarks on representative payloads (Rishi) — 512 & 1024 token runs, p95/p99 latency, and memory/kv stats
- 35–60m: Ops + migration path for Dedicated pool (Naomi covers config & traffic ramp)
- 60–85m: Cost sensitivity & batching/quantization levers (Marissa/Rishi)
- 85–90m: Action items & next steps

I'll attach a short eval checklist we use to correlate results to success criteria. If Sam can drop a small sample (5–10 payloads) in that Drive folder ahead of the meeting, I’ll pre-run and save time.

Attachment: eval-checklist.md

-Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Ben / Rishi / Naomi —

Thanks — that agenda looks good. Sam can drop the payload samples into the Drive folder by EOD today. Procurement confirmed they will review updated commercial terms on Dec 2; if all looks good we’ll queue signatures in the week of Dec 13.

We’re also comfortable with the proposed evaluation window and the success criteria you outlined. Please finalize the MAP with the milestones and a short checklist for our procurement team (pricing summary + list of deliverables). Once you push the updated MAP and the procurement checklist I’ll circulate internally and confirm the mid-December procurement slot.

Best,
Elena
